diagnostic_approaches.name: 2D X-ray fluoroscopy–guided bronchoscopic biopsy of peripheral pulmonary lesions
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Facilitate diagnostic biopsies of suspicious peripheral pulmonary lesions or segments with interstitial pathology under 2D X-ray guidance.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Advance instruments through the working channel beyond conventional bronchoscopic view under 2D X-ray fluoroscopy.
limitations: Coarse resolution of 2D X-ray imaging information in a 3D environment.
Does not give universal and unambiguous accurate guidance and outcome in peripheral pulmonary lesion diagnostics.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: lesions that were less than 20 mm, with a reported sensitivity of 14% and negative predictive value of 47% [1].

diagnostic_approaches.name: CBCT-based navigation bronchoscopy (stand-alone)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Use CBCT imaging and augmented fluoroscopy as a single tool for navigation and biopsy of small peripheral nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain CBCT spin on inspiratory breath-hold; segment lesion and intended pathway; use augmented fluoroscopy to advance an extended working channel to target. Confirm position with rEBUS and/or repeat CBCT before sampling.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Tool-in-lesion confirmation on CBCT and/or concentric rEBUS image indicates optimal sampling position.
limitations: Intermittent 3D imaging; divergence between breath-hold CBCT and ventilated fluoroscopy; movement/deformation from tools and ventilation may require additional spins.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: This workflow has a high diagnostic yield of 78.2% (95% CI 71.5–83.7, intermediate definition) as published in a meta-analysis.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Augmented fluoroscopy overlay methods
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Visually relay the obtained 3D information from the CBCT scan back onto live 2D fluoroscopy.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: 1) Place markers/lines on CBCT volume then overlay on AF; 2) Overlay full CBCT volume on AF and adjust transparency.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Augmented overlay shows segmented targets and instrument positions over live fluoroscopy.
limitations: Based on acquired 3D volume and not fully real-time.
Breath-hold CBCT vs ventilated fluoroscopy leads to mismatch.
Instrument/lung deformation can alter positions; may require additional scans.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Manually placing markers or lines on the CBCT volume ... selecting the overlay mode, as facilitated by the vendor software.

conclusion.text: CBCT (with AF on fixed systems) enables near real-time tool-in-lesion confirmation and high yield for small peripheral nodules; mobile systems can be integrated with RAB to mitigate CT-to-body divergence. Radiation exposure is comparable to diagnostic chest CT when optimized.
conclusion.source_excerpt: CBCT navigation bronchoscopy is safe, has a low complication rate and is a cost-effective clinical strategy.
